newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-YANKEES REACQUIRE MIKE STANLEY FROM RED SOX.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-YANKEES REACQUIRE MIKE STANLEY FROM RED SOX.

text.p: The New York Yankees, who have been shopping for right-handed power, reacquired fan favorite Mike Stanley from the Boston Red Sox Wednesday.

The 34-year-old Stanley, who hit a career-high 26 home runs for the Yankees in 1993, was traded to New York along with minor league infielder Randy Brown in exchange for minor league pitcher Tony Armas and a player to be named.

Though he caught for the Yankees in the past, Stanley is expected to be used primarily as a designated hitter. For the Red Sox this season, Stanley hit .300 with 13 homers and 53 RBI in 260 at-bats over 97 games.

"I'm happy that I'm going to a team that I'm used to playing for. I'm familiar with the surroundings, I know how to get to the ballpark," said Stanley, who will report to the Yankees in time for Thursday's game.

"It's very exciting, because they're right in the heat of a pennant race and they're in the lead for the wild card," Stanley said. "Obviously, coming off the World Series, people are still looking for a winner. Hopefully, I can provide some sort of help in the stretch.
"I guess I'm going to be a DH, especially after Cecil (Fielder) went down. I don't know if that means every day, or whether that means the same type of situation that was here -- platooning."

Yankees catcher Joe Girardi welcomed the move. "I think getting Mike Stanley is great," said Girardi. "He is an excellent right-handed hitter who always hits well at Yankee Stadium. He sent me a telegram when I first came here and was getting a rough time.
"I know he missed out on the World Series. Our goal is still the same as last year, no matter who is playing at a given time -- win the World Series again.
"Mike Stanley has a lot of friends here in this locker room and that's important. He will be a big help."
The Yankees were involved in trade talks for right-handed hitters Jose Canseco, Dante Bichette and Stanley before and after the July 31 trade deadline.

Unable to swing a deal before the deadline, Yankees general manager Bob Watson signed right-handed hitter Pete Incaviglia, who was released by Baltimore, to a minor-league contract. But Incaviglia was designated for assignment Tuesday night -- evidence that the Yankees were closing in on a deal.

Stanley signed a two-year deal with Boston after getting shunned by the Yankees before the 1996 season. After Joe Torre was named manager, he opted for free agent Girardi. The move was unpopular with the fans until Girardi helped New York's run to a World Series championship.
The 27-year-old Brown played 97 games with Double-A Trenton of the Eastern League and hit .256 with eight homers and 49 RBI. He struck out 102 times in 336 at-bats for the Thunder.

The right-handed Armas, a 6-foot-4 (1.93 metres), 175-pounder (79 kg), was 8-3 with a 2.12 earned run average in 18 starts between a pair of Class-A levels -- Greensboro and Tampa. After nine starts at each stop, Armas compiled 97 2/3 innings and allowed 79 hits and 29 walks with 90 strikeouts.

Armas is the 19-year-old son of the former Red Sox slugger by the same name. His father led the American League with 43 homers in 1984 and hit 115 homers for the Red Sox from 1983-86. He also played for the Oakland Athletics and hit 251 career homers.

"In Armas, naturally, we like the bloodlines," said Red Sox general manager Dan Duquette. "His dad had some great years here. We've scouted him, our scouts have followed him since he was a kid. We did try to sign him as an amateur, but the Yankees signed him.
"This year, he has put together a good year between Greensboro and Tampa. We think he has a chance to be a solid major-league starter in the future."
